# package server

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-dnp3/server"
```

Package server is the DNP3 outstation (IEEE 1815-2012).

A [Server](#type-server) holds a [Database](#type-database) of points (binary, double-bit, counters, frozen counters, analogs, frozen analogs, outputs, octet strings) whose changes become events in classes 1 to 3, buffered per master (association) and reported in polls and unsolicited responses. Controls, restarts, time synchronization and the application functions go to the [Handler](#type-handler) of [WithHandler](#func-withhandler) and its optional interfaces; file transfer to the [FileServer](#type-fileserver) of [WithFileServer](#func-withfileserver).

Device attributes are [WithAttributes](#func-withattributes) (set 0) and [WithAttributeSet](#func-withattributeset); FREEZE\_AT\_TIME requests are scheduled (MaxScheduledFreezes).

Transports: [Server.ListenAndServe](#func-server-listenandserve) and [Server.Serve](#func-server-serve) for TCP, TLS with [WithTLS](#func-withtls), [Server.ServeUDP](#func-server-serveudp) for UDP, [Server.ServeConn](#func-server-serveconn) for any byte stream such as a serial port, and [Server.DialAndServe](#func-server-dialandserve) for the dual end point, where the outstation connects to its master. [Server.Close](#func-server-close) ends them all. A [Group](#type-group) serves several outstations, each a Server at its own link address, on the same port or line (multi-drop).

Secure Authentication version 5 ([WithSecureAuthentication](#func-withsecureauthentication)) challenges critical requests, takes part in the session key change, accepts aggressive mode requests and keeps the security statistics (g121, g122) per master.

API.md lists the whole API; INTEROPERABILITY.md what is implemented, clause by clause.

## Constants

```go
const (
	DefaultExpectedKeyChangeInterval = 30 * time.Minute
	DefaultExpectedKeyChangeCount    = 2000
	DefaultMaxKeyStatusRequests      = 5
)
```

The defaults of the expected session key change (IEEE 1815-2012 clause 7.6.1.4.5, which recommends twice the master's 15 minutes and 1000 messages) and of the maximum session key status count (7.6.1.4.6).

```go
const DefaultEventLimit = 100
```

DefaultEventLimit is the number of events of each point type an association buffers when no limit is configured.

```go
const DefaultFileTimeout = 5 * time.Minute
```

DefaultFileTimeout is how long an open file may go without a request naming its handle before the outstation closes it (IEEE 1815-2012 4.4.17.1.1, p. 67), when WithFileTimeout does not set it.

```go
const DefaultPort = 20000
```

DefaultPort is the registered DNP3 port.

```go
const DefaultReplyTimeout = 2 * time.Second
```

DefaultReplyTimeout is how long a challenge waits for its reply when SecureAuth.ReplyTimeout is zero: 2 seconds (IEEE 1815-2012 clause 7.6.1.4.1).

```go
const DefaultTLSPort = 19999
```

DefaultTLSPort is the port of DNP3 over TLS: IEEE 1815-2012 clause 7.8.8 makes 19999 the default, and clause 13.2.2.2 requires devices that use TLS to support it.

```go
const MaxScheduledFreezes = 16
```

MaxScheduledFreezes is how many FREEZE\_AT\_TIME schedules the outstation keeps at once; a request for more is refused. A schedule belongs to the Server: a periodic one keeps its place until a new FREEZE\_AT\_TIME for its points or Close, whatever happens to the master's connection.

## Functions

### func ServeByMasterIP

```go
func ServeByMasterIP(l net.Listener, routes ...Route) error
```

ServeByMasterIP accepts connections on l and gives each to the route of the master's IP address: method 1 of IEEE 1815-2012 clause 13.2.3.5.1, which clause 13.2.3.5.4 requires of an outstation that supports multiple masters. The first route whose prefix holds the address takes the connection; one that no route takes is closed. Method 2, a port for each master, is a listener for each Server or Group.

The targets serve the connections as their own Serve does, with their TLS handshake, WithMaxConnections and WithMasterIPs; give l a listener of tls.NewListener for TLS. Closing a target closes its connections; closing l stops the accepting. ServeByMasterIP returns the error that stopped l, wrapping net.ErrClosed after l.Close.

	l, _ := net.Listen("tcp", ":20000")
	go server.ServeByMasterIP(l,
		server.Route{Masters: netip.MustParsePrefix("192.0.2.1/32"), Server: scada},
		server.Route{Masters: netip.MustParsePrefix("198.51.100.0/24"), Group: engineering})

## Types

### type ActivateConfigHandler

```go
type ActivateConfigHandler interface {
	ActivateConfig(ctx context.Context, headers []app.Header) (app.ActivateConfigStatus, app.IIN)
}
```

ActivateConfigHandler is an optional interface of the [Handler](#type-handler) for ACTIVATE\_CONFIG (function code 31). When the handler implements it, ACTIVATE\_CONFIG goes to ActivateConfig instead of [ApplicationHandler](#type-applicationhandler).

headers are the request's objects: file specifications (g70v8, as app.FileSpecification) or octet strings (g110) that name the configurations to activate. ActivateConfig returns the status of requested operation and the IIN2 error bits of the response. Without an error bit the response carries the status in one g91v1 object with qualifier 0x07 (count 1); with one, the response has no object. A status that does not encode (app.ActivateConfigStatus.Raw) or does not fit the largest response fragment is answered with IIN2.2 (PARAMETER\_ERROR).

ActivateConfig checks the request; it does not activate. IEEE 1815-2012 4.4.20 (p. 78) has the outstation complete the transmission of the g91v1 response before it starts the activation, and activate nothing when a check fails. The outstation sends the response after ActivateConfig returns, so a handler starts the activation after that, for example from a goroutine. The response's IIN reflect the current conditions: the handler does not set IIN2.5 for a failed check, and IIN1.7 is set by the restart itself, not in anticipation of it.

### type ApplicationHandler

```go
type ApplicationHandler interface {
	Application(ctx context.Context, fc app.FunctionCode, headers []app.Header) app.IIN
}
```

ApplicationHandler is an optional interface of the [Handler](#type-handler) for the function codes that act on the outstation's applications: INITIALIZE\_DATA, INITIALIZE\_APPL, START\_APPL, STOP\_APPL, SAVE\_CONFIG and ACTIVATE\_CONFIG. It returns the IIN2 bits of the response: the request errors IIN2.0 to IIN2.2, or 0 for success, and IIN2.4 (ALREADY\_EXECUTING, IEEE 1815-2012 4.5.13, p. 87) while the operation requested is still running; other bits are ignored. Without it these functions are answered with IIN2.0.

A successful SAVE\_CONFIG is answered with a time delay of 0 (g52v2, 4.4.12, p. 60): the handler has saved the configuration when it returns. INITIALIZE\_DATA is obsolete, and new designs shall not implement it (4.4.10, p. 58): a handler returns app.IINNoFuncCodeSupport for it.

### type Command

```go
type Command struct {
	// GV is the object of the control: app.G12V1 (control relay output
	// block), app.G12V2 (pattern control block) or app.G41V1..app.G41V4
	// (analog output block).
	GV app.GroupVariation
	// Index is the point index.
	Index uint32
	// Value is an app.CROB or an app.AnalogOutput. Its Status field is
	// zero: a control whose request carries another status does not reach
	// the Handler. NON_PARTICIPATING (126) is echoed unchanged (IEEE
	// 1815-2012 Table 11-7 footnote a, p. 330), any other status is
	// answered with FORMAT_ERROR (TB2014-002), and a CROB with the queue
	// bit set with NOT_SUPPORTED (A.8.1.2.2, p. 506).
	//
	// A CROB with Count 0 is passed on as it came. IEEE 1815-2012
	// A.8.1.2.2 (p. 506) makes support for it optional; an outstation that
	// supports it does not change the output, ignores the on and off
	// times and returns the status it would have returned. That is the
	// Handler's to do.
	Value app.Value
	// Master is the link address of the master that sent the control.
	Master link.Address
}
```

Command is one control a master sent.

#### func (Database) AddFrozenAnalogInput

```go
func (db *Database) AddFrozenAnalogInput(index uint32, cfg PointConfig, v app.Analog) error
```

AddFrozenAnalogInput adds a frozen analog input (groups 31 and 33). A freeze request copies the analog input of the same index into it and, with an event class, raises a frozen analog input event at every freeze (IEEE 1815-2012 11.9.1.2, p. 333). Add that analog input too, as the database does not check it; one without it is never frozen.

#### func (Database) AddFrozenCounter

```go
func (db *Database) AddFrozenCounter(index uint32, cfg PointConfig, v app.Counter) error
```

AddFrozenCounter adds a frozen counter (groups 21 and 23). A freeze request copies the counter of the same index into it and, with an event class, raises a frozen counter event at every freeze (IEEE 1815-2012 11.9.5.2, p. 341). A frozen counter is the frozen value of the counter of its index: add that counter too, as the database does not check it; one without it is never frozen.

### type Dialer

```go
type Dialer interface {
	DialContext(ctx context.Context, network, addr string) (net.Conn, error)
}
```

Dialer opens the TCP connections of DialAndServe; \*net.Dialer satisfies it, as does a proxy's or a jump host's DialContext. It has the shape of client.Dialer.

Like net.Dialer, a Dialer returns a non-nil connection exactly when the error is nil: one that returns neither fails the attempt, and a connection returned together with an error is closed. It must honour ctx, which carries the dial timeout (10 seconds) and ends when the context of DialAndServe does or the server is closed.

### type Group

```go
type Group struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Group serves several outstations on the same connections: a multi-drop channel (IEEE 1815-2012 clause 9), where every station takes the frames to its own link address and all of them the broadcasts. Each outstation is a [Server](#type-server) with its own address, database, handler and options; the group only shares the listeners and connections, so that a master reaches each by its address over one port or one serial line.

#### func NewGroup

```go
func NewGroup(servers ...*Server) (*Group, error)
```

NewGroup returns a group of servers, which must have distinct addresses. The servers are served through the group: do not serve them on their own as well.

#### func (Group) Close

```go
func (g *Group) Close() error
```

Close stops the listeners and closes every server of the group, and with them the connections.

#### func (Group) ListenAndServe

```go
func (g *Group) ListenAndServe(addr string) error
```

ListenAndServe listens on the TCP address addr, with the TLS configuration of the first server's WithTLS when it has one, and serves until Close. An empty addr is ":20000", or ":19999" (DefaultTLSPort) with TLS.

#### func (Group) Serve

```go
func (g *Group) Serve(l net.Listener) error
```

Serve accepts connections on l and serves each until Close. A connection is refused while the group holds as many as the smallest WithMaxConnections of its servers. It returns nil after Close, otherwise the error that stopped the listener.

#### func (Group) ServeConn

```go
func (g *Group) ServeConn(rw io.ReadWriteCloser, remote net.Addr) error
```

ServeConn serves one stream, for example a serial port, for every outstation of the group until it ends or the group is closed.

```go

```

ServeUDP serves the outstations of the group over UDP on pc, as [Server.ServeUDP](#func-server-serveudp) does for one.

#### func (Group) Servers

```go
func (g *Group) Servers() []*Server
```

Servers returns the servers of the group, in the order given.

### type Handler

```go
type Handler interface {
	// Select checks whether the control could be executed now, without
	// executing it.
	Select(ctx context.Context, c Command) app.CommandStatus

	// Operate executes the control.
	Operate(ctx context.Context, c Command, op OperateType) app.CommandStatus
}
```

Handler executes controls. Its methods are called on the goroutine of the master's association, one request at a time per master; a slow handler delays that master's requests, not the others'.

The returned status is echoed to the master. A handler that does not support a point returns app.StatusNotSupported; the response then also sets IIN2.2 (PARAMETER\_ERROR).

A handler, and every optional handler interface, must not call [Server.Close](#func-server-close) itself: Close waits for the association goroutine the handler runs on. Call it from another goroutine (go srv.Close()); ctx is canceled when the server closes.

### type Link

```go
type Link struct {
	// Confirmed sends user data as CONFIRMED_USER_DATA. Set it on serial
	// links only: IEEE 1815-2012 clause 13.2.1.1 forbids confirmed link
	// frames over TCP and UDP, and a channel on a network stream with it
	// logs a warning. The default is UNCONFIRMED_USER_DATA.
	Confirmed bool
	// Timeout is the wait for a link layer answer. Zero means 2 seconds.
	Timeout time.Duration
	// Retries is the number of repeats of an unanswered primary frame.
	Retries int
	// KeepAlive is the idle time after which REQUEST_LINK_STATUS is sent
	// (the keep-alive of IEEE 1815-2012 clause 13.2.3.3.1); a peer that
	// does not answer it ends the connection. Zero means 60 seconds; any
	// positive duration is taken. A negative value disables it, which the
	// clause allows for testing only: in service, set a long interval
	// instead.
	KeepAlive time.Duration
}
```

Link configures the data link layer.

### type Option

```go
type Option func(*options) error
```

Option configures a [Server](#type-server).

#### func WithAddress

```go
func WithAddress(a link.Address) Option
```

WithAddress sets the link address of the outstation. The default is 10.

#### func WithAttributeSet

```go
func WithAttributeSet(set uint16, attrs map[uint8]app.Attribute, writable ...uint8) Option
```

WithAttributeSet sets the device attributes of another set (group 0, the set is the index; IEEE 1815-2012 clause 11.9.1), keyed by variation. The variations in writable can be written by a master, with a value of the same type: the outstation stores it and, when the [Handler](#type-handler) implements [AttributeSetWriteHandler](#type-attributesetwritehandler), tells it first. Other writes are refused. The attributes' data is copied.

#### func WithAttributes

```go
func WithAttributes(attrs map[uint8]app.Attribute) Option
```

WithAttributes sets the device attributes of set 0 (group 0) the outstation reports, keyed by variation, for example app.AttrManufacturerName. The list of attribute variations (g0v255) is built from them; an attribute is writable when the [Handler](#type-handler) implements [WriteHandler](#type-writehandler). The attributes' data is copied.

#### func WithConfirmTimeout

```go
func WithConfirmTimeout(d time.Duration) Option
```

WithConfirmTimeout sets how long the outstation waits for the application confirmation of a response or unsolicited response. The default is 5 seconds.

#### func WithDeadbandIntegerOnly

```go
func WithDeadbandIntegerOnly(enabled bool) Option
```

WithDeadbandIntegerOnly reports analog input deadbands (group 34) in variations 1 and 2 only, for masters without floating point, as IEEE 1815-2012 A.18.3.2.3 (p. 609) requires a device that reports variation 3 to be configurable: a deadband is rounded to the nearest integer and limited to 4294967295, and a READ of g34v3 is answered with IIN2.1. Masters can still write any variation.

#### func WithDialer

```go
func WithDialer(d Dialer) Option
```

WithDialer sets the dialer of DialAndServe: it is called with network "tcp" and the address given to DialAndServe, and with WithTLS the TLS handshake runs over the connection it returns (tls.Client). Use it to bind a source address, dial through a proxy, or refuse addresses (see SECURITY.md: an allowlist belongs in the dialer, for example in net.Dialer.Control, which sees the resolved IP). The listeners of ListenAndServe, Serve, ServeConn and the UDP functions do not dial and are not affected. nil keeps the default, a net.Dialer with a 10 second timeout.

#### func WithEventLimits

```go
func WithEventLimits(limits map[PointType]int) Option
```

WithEventLimits sets the number of events of each point type an association buffers; types not named keep DefaultEventLimit. When a buffer is full the oldest event of the type is discarded and the outstation reports IIN2.3 (EVENT\_BUFFER\_OVERFLOW) until the master has confirmed enough events for every buffer that lost one to have room for another (IEEE 1815-2012 4.5.12). A limit of 0 buffers no event of the type: an event of it with a class is lost, and IIN2.3 then stays set until a restart; give such points class 0 instead.

#### func WithFileServer

```go
func WithFileServer(fs FileServer) Option
```

WithFileServer serves file transfer (group 70) from fs.

#### func WithFileTimeout

```go
func WithFileTimeout(timeout time.Duration, class Class) Option
```

WithFileTimeout sets how long an open file may go without a request naming its handle; the default is DefaultFileTimeout. The outstation then closes it, aborted, and reports a file transport status event (g70v6) with status HANDLE\_EXPIRED in the event class (1..3, the default 1), as IEEE 1815-2012 4.4.17.1.1 (p. 67) and 5.3.8 Rule 12 (p. 120) require; the timeout must be configurable up to one hour.

```go
func WithHandler(h Handler) Option
```

WithHandler sets the handler for controls and, through its optional interfaces, for restarts, time synchronization, application functions and writes. The default supports no control.


WithLink configures the data link layer.

#### func WithLogger

```go
func WithLogger(l dnp3.Logger) Option
```

WithLogger sets the logger; logging is silent by default.

#### func WithMasterIPs

```go
func WithMasterIPs(prefixes ...netip.Prefix) Option
```

WithMasterIPs limits the masters to those whose IP address lies in one of prefixes: a TCP connection from another address is closed when it is accepted, and a UDP datagram from another address is ignored. The default accepts any address. IEEE 1815-2012 clause 13.2.3.2.2 d requires an outstation to be configurable to accept UDP requests only from specific master IP addresses, and clause 13.2.3.1.4 a recommends the same validation of TCP connection requests. A single address is a prefix of its full length, such as netip.MustParsePrefix("192.0.2.7/32").

The check applies to Serve, ListenAndServe, ServeUDP, ServeUDPTo and ServeUDPFixed; ServeConn serves the stream it is given.

#### func WithMasters

```go
func WithMasters(addrs ...link.Address) Option
```

WithMasters restricts the masters the outstation answers to these link addresses. Their associations, and so their event buffers, exist from the start: events are kept while a master is not connected. Without it any master is answered and its association is created on first contact.

#### func WithMaxConnections

```go
func WithMaxConnections(n int) Option
```

WithMaxConnections limits concurrent connections; further ones are closed at once. An accepted connection counts from the moment it is accepted, also during its TLS handshake. The default is 16.

#### func WithMaxControls

```go
func WithMaxControls(n int) Option
```

WithMaxControls sets how many controls one request may carry; the controls beyond it are answered with TOO\_MANY\_OBJS. Every point a pattern control block (g12v2 with its mask g12v3) operates counts as a control: the block carries out those within the limit and is answered with TOO\_MANY\_OBJS when its mask names more. The default is 16.

#### func WithMaxFragment

```go
func WithMaxFragment(tx, rx int) Option
```

WithMaxFragment sets the largest response fragment the outstation sends (tx) and the largest request it reassembles (rx). The defaults are 2048; IEEE 1815-2012 requires at least 249.

#### func WithMetrics

```go
func WithMetrics(m dnp3.Metrics) Option
```

WithMetrics sets the metrics callbacks. A value that also implements dnp3.ServerMetrics receives the server-level callbacks.

#### func WithSecureAuthentication

```go
func WithSecureAuthentication(cfg SecureAuth) Option
```

WithSecureAuthentication enables Secure Authentication: critical requests are executed only after the master answered a challenge with the right MAC, or when they carry it themselves in aggressive mode. The outstation takes part in the session key change and keeps the security statistics (g121, g122) per master. A user number of 0, which IEEE 1815-2012 reserves for an unknown user, is taken as 1, the default user. The keys are copied: the caller may clear its own slices afterwards.

#### func WithSelectTimeout

```go
func WithSelectTimeout(d time.Duration) Option
```

WithSelectTimeout sets how long a SELECT stays valid for its OPERATE; an OPERATE after it is answered with TIMEOUT. The default is 10 seconds.

#### func WithSelfAddress

```go
func WithSelfAddress(enabled bool) Option
```

WithSelfAddress makes the outstation accept frames sent to the self address 0xFFFC as if they were sent to its own address.

#### func WithTLS

```go
func WithTLS(cfg *tls.Config) Option
```

WithTLS serves TLS (IEEE 1815-2012 Annex B / IEC 62351-3) on the listeners of ListenAndServe, and is the TLS client configuration of DialAndServe. Serve and ServeConn take the connection as it is.

#### func WithTimeSync

```go
func WithTimeSync(interval time.Duration) Option
```

WithTimeSync makes the outstation request time synchronization (IIN1.4 NEED\_TIME) at start and again when interval has passed since the last one. Zero, the default, never requests it.

Its time counts as unsynchronized, which relative-time events report with a g51v2 CTO instead of g51v1, until the first synchronization after the start or a restart, and again once twice the interval has passed without one.

#### func WithUnsolicited

```go
func WithUnsolicited(u Unsolicited) Option
```

WithUnsolicited configures unsolicited responses; they are disabled by default.

### type PointConfig

```go
type PointConfig struct {
	// Class is the event class, 0..3. Events are only produced for 1..3.
	Class Class

	// StaticVariation is the variation of the point in class 0 and in
	// reads of "any variation"; 0 selects the type's default (g1v2, g3v2,
	// g10v2, g20v1, g21v1, g30v1, g31v1, g40v1).
	StaticVariation uint8

	// EventVariation is the variation of the point's events; 0 selects
	// the default (g2v2, g4v2, g11v2, g22v5, g23v5, g32v3, g33v3, g42v3).
	EventVariation uint8

	// Deadband applies to counters, frozen counters and analog points: a
	// change of the value produces an event only when it exceeds the
	// deadband. Flag changes always produce one. It must be a finite number
	// of at least zero; Add refuses NaN, infinity and negative deadbands, and
	// a WRITE of one is answered with IIN2.2.
	Deadband float64

	// ExcludeFromClass0 leaves the point out of class 0 responses; it can
	// still be read by group and variation.
	ExcludeFromClass0 bool

	// CommandEventClass, for binary and analog outputs, reports every
	// OPERATE, DIRECT_OPERATE and DIRECT_OPERATE_NR of the point as a
	// command event in that class: g13 (the commanded state) or g43 (the
	// commanded value) with the status the handler returned. 0 reports
	// none.
	CommandEventClass Class

	// CommandEventVariation is the variation of the command events; 0
	// selects g13v2 or g43v3 (with time).
	CommandEventVariation uint8
}
```

PointConfig configures one point.

### type PointType

```go
type PointType uint8
```

PointType is a kind of point in the [Database](#type-database).

```go
const (
	BinaryInput PointType = iota
	DoubleBitInput
	BinaryOutput
	Counter
	FrozenCounter
	AnalogInput
	FrozenAnalogInput
	AnalogOutput
	OctetString
	// SecurityStatistic are the Secure Authentication statistics (group
	// 121, events group 122). The outstation keeps them per association
	// when secure authentication is on; they cannot be added to the
	// database.
	SecurityStatistic
	// BinaryOutputCommand and AnalogOutputCommand are the command events
	// (groups 13 and 43) of the outputs whose PointConfig has a
	// CommandEventClass. They have no static objects and cannot be added
	// to the database.
	BinaryOutputCommand
	AnalogOutputCommand
	// TimeAndInterval are indexed absolute times with an interval (g50v4,
	// app.AbsoluteTime with Units), for example a schedule. They have no
	// events and no class.
	TimeAndInterval
	// fileStatusEvent are the file transport status events (g70v6) of the
	// files the outstation closed on its own (IEEE 1815-2012 4.4.17.1.1):
	// internal, with no points and no static objects.

)
```

Point types.

#### func (PointType) String

```go
func (t PointType) String() string
```

String returns the name of the point type, for example "analog input".

### type Redial

```go
type Redial struct {
	// MinDelay is the delay after the first failure; it doubles after each
	// further one. Zero means 1 second.
	MinDelay time.Duration
	// MaxDelay caps the delay. Zero means 1 minute.
	MaxDelay time.Duration
	// Jitter randomizes each delay, so that outstations that lost their
	// connections together do not reconnect together: a fraction from 0
	// to 1, each delay is drawn uniformly from [(1-Jitter)·d, d] of the
	// delay d that doubles. Zero, the default, waits d exactly. It has the
	// semantics of client.Reconnect.Jitter.
	Jitter float64
}
```

Redial configures how DialAndServe reconnects: with exponential backoff between failed attempts.

### type RestartHandler

```go
type RestartHandler interface {
	// Restart schedules a restart and returns the time after which the
	// master may poll again. The outstation answers before the restart
	// takes place; restarting the process (or calling Server.Restart) is
	// up to the handler. A non-nil error refuses the restart.
	Restart(ctx context.Context, cold bool) (time.Duration, error)
}
```

RestartHandler is an optional interface of the [Handler](#type-handler): without it, COLD\_RESTART and WARM\_RESTART are answered with IIN2.0 (NO\_FUNC\_CODE\_SUPPORT).

### type Route

```go
type Route struct {
	Masters netip.Prefix
	Server  *Server
	Group   *Group
}
```

A Route assigns the connections of the masters whose IP address lies in Masters to one outstation, Server, or to the outstations of one Group. Exactly one of Server and Group is set.

### type SecureAuth

```go
type SecureAuth struct {
	// User is the user and its key.
	User secauth.User
	// Critical are the function codes the outstation challenges. Nil
	// selects DefaultCritical. The codes Table 7-7 marks MANDATORY
	// (secauth.MandatoryCritical) are challenged whatever the list says
	// (clause 7.5.2.3.2 a): a list without them is completed with them.
	Critical []app.FunctionCode
	// ReplyTimeout is how long a challenge waits for the master's reply
	// (clause 7.6.1.4.1). When it expires, the challenged request is
	// discarded and counted as a reply timeout; past Max Reply Timeouts
	// the session keys become invalid (COMM_FAIL, Table 7-8). Zero selects
	// DefaultReplyTimeout.
	ReplyTimeout time.Duration
	// StatisticsClass is the event class of security statistic events
	// (g122); zero selects class 1. StatisticsThreshold, when set (at most
	// 65 535), is the event threshold of every statistic Thresholds does
	// not name: the number of increments between two of its events.
	StatisticsClass     Class
	StatisticsThreshold uint32
	// Thresholds sets the event threshold (1..65 535) of single statistics
	// (clause 7.6.1.4.2). A statistic neither names nor StatisticsThreshold
	// covers has the default of IEEE 1815-2012 Table 7-6
	// (secauth.Statistic.DefaultThreshold). The thresholds of
	// authentication failures, reply timeouts, rekeys due to authentication
	// failure and error messages sent are also the steps of the maxima the
	// state machine acts on (Table 7-15): for example, error messages stop
	// once Error Messages Sent exceeds Max Error Messages Sent, until the
	// next valid session key change.
	Thresholds map[secauth.Statistic]uint16
	// NoAggressiveMode refuses aggressive mode requests (clause 7.6.1.4.7):
	// they are discarded and, within Max Error Messages Sent, answered with
	// error 4, aggressive mode not supported.
	NoAggressiveMode bool
	// ExpectedKeyChangeInterval is how long session keys stay valid
	// without a session key change (clause 7.6.1.4.5): once it has passed,
	// the key status is NOT_INIT until the master changes them. Zero
	// selects DefaultExpectedKeyChangeInterval; a negative value disables
	// the interval, leaving ExpectedKeyChangeCount. It does not apply to a
	// pre-shared session key.
	ExpectedKeyChangeInterval time.Duration
	// ExpectedKeyChangeCount is how many authentication messages
	// (challenges, replies and aggressive mode requests) the session keys
	// serve before they become invalid without a session key change
	// (clause 7.6.1.4.5). Zero selects DefaultExpectedKeyChangeCount.
	ExpectedKeyChangeCount uint32
	// MaxKeyStatusRequests is how many session key status requests the
	// outstation takes within the expected key change interval before it
	// reports, as an error in its log, that the limit was exceeded
	// (clause 7.6.1.4.6). The requests are still answered. 2..255; zero
	// selects DefaultMaxKeyStatusRequests.
	MaxKeyStatusRequests int
}
```

SecureAuth configures DNP3 Secure Authentication version 5 (see package secauth): with an update key, the master negotiates the session keys with the session key change; without, a pre-shared session key is used.

The outstation is the challenger of IEEE 1815-2012 Table 7-8, for one user per master (association).

### type Server

```go
type Server struct {

	// timeSync is the synchronization state of clock.

	// handles assigns file handles, unique to the outstation.

	// FREEZE_AT_TIME schedules, by the points they name
	// pending counts the connections Serve and ServeByMasterIP accepted
	// that are not among channels yet, in their TLS handshake: they count
	// against WithMaxConnections from the moment they are accepted.

	// closeCtx is canceled by Close: it ends the TLS handshakes of accepted
	// connections.

}
```

Server is a DNP3 outstation: a point database served to masters over any number of channels.

#### func New

```go
func New(opts ...Option) (*Server, error)
```

New returns an outstation configured by opts. Add points to its Database, then serve it with ListenAndServe, Serve or ServeConn.

#### func (Server) Address

```go
func (s *Server) Address() link.Address
```

Address returns the link address of the outstation.

#### func (Server) Close

```go
func (s *Server) Close() error
```

Close stops the listeners, closes every connection, ends the TLS handshakes in progress and stops the associations. It waits for their goroutines to end, so it must not be called from a [Handler](#type-handler) method, which runs on an association goroutine: call go srv.Close() there.

#### func (Server) CloseConnections

```go
func (s *Server) CloseConnections()
```

CloseConnections closes every current client connection without stopping the listeners: masters may reconnect. Associations and their event buffers are kept.

#### func (Server) Database

```go
func (s *Server) Database() *Database
```

Database returns the point database.

#### func (Server) DialAndServe

```go
func (s *Server) DialAndServe(ctx context.Context, addr string, r Redial) error
```

DialAndServe is the outstation's end of a TCP connection that the outstation establishes (the dual end point of IEEE 1815-2012 clause 13.2.3.1.3, for an outstation behind a firewall or on a dial-out link): it connects to the master at addr, with TLS when WithTLS was given (the outstation is then the TLS client: the configuration's RootCAs verify the master, its Certificates are presented, ServerName defaults to the host of addr), serves the connection like an accepted one, and connects again when it ends, with the delays of r. It returns when ctx is done (ctx.Err()) or the server is closed (nil).

Only one connection to the master stands at a time, and the master's own has priority (clause 13.2.3.1.3): while a master is connected to the server's listener, DialAndServe does not connect, and checks again every r.MinDelay.

The connection is opened by the dialer of WithDialer, by default a net.Dialer. A failed attempt is logged with an error that wraps dnp3.ErrConnectFailed and the dialer's error. DialAndServe fails with dnp3.ErrInvalidOption when r.Jitter is not within \[0, 1].

#### func (Server) ListenAndServe

```go
func (s *Server) ListenAndServe(addr string) error
```

ListenAndServe listens on the TCP address addr, with TLS when WithTLS was given, and serves until Close. An empty addr is ":20000", or ":19999" (DefaultTLSPort) with TLS.

#### func (Server) Now

```go
func (s *Server) Now() time.Time
```

Now returns the time of the outstation's clock, which time synchronization sets.

#### func (Server) Restart

```go
func (s *Server) Restart()
```

Restart behaves as after a restart of the outstation: every association reports IIN1.7 (DEVICE\_RESTART) again, its event buffer is cleared, unsolicited responses start over with a null unsolicited response, and, with WithTimeSync, its time counts as unsynchronized until the next time synchronization (IIN1.4). Points get the classes they were added with again, undoing ASSIGN\_CLASS (IEEE 1815-2012 4.4.14, p. 63); deadbands written by a master are kept.

#### func (Server) Serve

```go
func (s *Server) Serve(l net.Listener) error
```

Serve accepts connections on l and serves each until Close. It returns nil after Close, otherwise the error that stopped the listener.

#### func (Server) ServeConn

```go
func (s *Server) ServeConn(rw io.ReadWriteCloser, remote net.Addr) error
```

ServeConn serves one stream, for example a serial port or a connection accepted elsewhere, until it ends or the server is closed. remote names the peer in logs and metrics and may be nil. It returns the reason the stream ended: nil after Close.

#### func (Server) ServeUDP

```go
func (s *Server) ServeUDP(pc net.PacketConn) error
```

ServeUDP serves DNP3 over UDP on pc until Close. Each datagram carries link frames; responses go to the address the last datagram came from, so one socket serves one master at a time (a master behind another address takes over the socket when it sends).

Until a master has sent a datagram there is nowhere to send to: what the outstation sends before (the null unsolicited response, for one) is dropped, as an unreachable datagram would be, and repeated by the unsolicited retries. Use ServeUDPTo to name the master's address up front.

#### func (Server) ServeUDPFixed

```go
func (s *Server) ServeUDPFixed(pc net.PacketConn, peer net.Addr) error
```

ServeUDPFixed serves DNP3 over UDP on pc with responses always sent to peer, the master's address and port: case 1 of IEEE 1815-2012 Table 13-1, "send responses to a fixed port at the master", where ServeUDP is case 2 (reply to the port the request came from). Datagrams are taken from peer's IP address only, from any of its ports; WithMasterIPs, when given, applies as well.

#### func (Server) ServeUDPTo

```go
func (s *Server) ServeUDPTo(pc net.PacketConn, peer net.Addr) error
```

ServeUDPTo is ServeUDP with the master's address known from the start: unsolicited responses reach it before it sent anything. A datagram from another address takes over the socket, as with ServeUDP.

#### func (Server) SetIndications

```go
func (s *Server) SetIndications(bits app.IIN, on bool)
```

SetIndications sets or clears the application controlled internal indications of every association: app.IINLocalControl, app.IINDeviceTrouble and app.IINConfigCorrupt. Other bits are ignored.

### type TimeHandler

```go
type TimeHandler interface {
	SetTime(ctx context.Context, t time.Time)
}
```

TimeHandler is an optional interface of the [Handler](#type-handler). The outstation keeps its own clock, set by time synchronization; a TimeHandler is told of every synchronization as well, for example to set the device clock.

### type Unsolicited

```go
type Unsolicited struct {
	// Enabled allows unsolicited responses. When set, the outstation sends
	// a null unsolicited response when a master connects and reports
	// events of the classes the master enables (or of Classes from the
	// start).
	Enabled bool
	// Classes are the classes (1..3) the outstation reports unsolicited
	// before any ENABLE_UNSOLICITED, once the master has confirmed the
	// null unsolicited response. This departs from IEEE 1815-2012, under
	// which an outstation sends no data unsolicited until the master
	// enables it with ENABLE_UNSOLICITED (5.1.1.1.1 Rule 3, p. 101;
	// 4.4.13, p. 60). It is meant for masters that never send
	// ENABLE_UNSOLICITED; leave it empty, the default, for a master that
	// enables the classes it wants.
	Classes []Class
	// HoldTime is how long new events are collected before they are sent
	// unsolicited. Zero sends at once.
	HoldTime time.Duration
	// HoldCount sends at once when this many events are pending, before
	// HoldTime has passed. Zero means no count trigger.
	HoldCount int
	// Retries is how often an unconfirmed unsolicited response is
	// repeated before it is given up; its events are kept and reported
	// later. Zero means 3; a negative value repeats it until it is
	// confirmed.
	Retries int
	// RetryDelay is the pause after an unsolicited response was given up.
	// Zero means 5 seconds.
	RetryDelay time.Duration
}
```

Unsolicited configures unsolicited responses.

### type WriteHandler

```go
type WriteHandler interface {
	WriteAttribute(ctx context.Context, variation uint8, a app.Attribute) error
	WriteOctetString(ctx context.Context, index uint32, data []byte) error
}
```

WriteHandler is an optional interface of the [Handler](#type-handler) for WRITE requests on objects the outstation does not handle itself: device attributes (group 0) and octet strings (group 110). The outstation stores a written octet string in its database before it calls WriteOctetString. Errors are answered with IIN2.2 (PARAMETER\_ERROR).
